clue.text: Sort of dive executed by fish?

definitions.meaning: a jackknife position in diving, body bent at the hips with legs straight

explanation.surface: A diving move is performed by a fish, as though fish entered diving contests.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a diving position with straight legs and a predatory freshwater fish; the question mark flags the playful pairing.

clue.text: Father's game: means to travel overseas

parts.note: pa is father, with the possessive s
a sport is a game

explanation.surface: Dad's favourite game is a way to see the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The official document a traveller must carry to cross international borders.

clue.text: Jack, King — simple to discard one

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: the word for simple throws away a letter

parts.note: naive means simple or unsophisticated
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A card player holding the jack and king finds it easy to throw one away.
explanation.definitionFit: In playing cards the jack is also called by this older name, which also means a rogue.

clue.text: Think about cut in insurance

indicators.note: the word for cutting is placed in the middle of the word for insurance

parts.note: cover is insurance protection
to hew is to cut with an axe

explanation.surface: Someone ponders a reduction in their insurance policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym: to mull something over at length, ruminating on it.

clue.text: Silver brought into house for show of respect

indicators.note: the symbol for silver is placed inside the word for house

parts.note: a home is a house
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Bringing the family silver home is a mark of reverence.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: honour or tribute paid publicly to someone.

clue.text: Gale: bird has to move gradually on part of building

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind
an owl is a bird
to edge is to inch along slowly

explanation.surface: In a strong wind, a bird must inch along a building's ledge.
explanation.definitionFit: The sill beneath a window, a projecting shelf that forms part of a building.

clue.text: One-third of vegans wrong to get upset about meat

indicators.note: the first two of the six letters of vegans are taken
in a down clue, the word for wrong is turned upside down

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Some vegans are dismayed to discover meat in their food.
explanation.walkthrough: VE plus SIN reversed (NIS) plus ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The meat of deer, a specific kind of game meat.

clue.text: Beams, extra money being announced

indicators.note: the word is spoken out, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: a raise is an increase in pay

explanation.surface: An employee is all smiles at hearing that their pay has gone up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: shafts of light, narrow streams of radiation.

clue.text: Small thing I included in complete sports venue

indicators.note: the small thing and I are put within the word for complete

parts.note: a sum is a complete total
a tad is a tiny amount

explanation.surface: A tiny item is fitted into a finished sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complete' looks like an adjective for the venue but supplies SUM, a complete total; 'included in' puts the small thing and I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A large arena with tiered seating where football and athletics are played.

clue.text: Inability to bear being hypnotised, interrupted by bullring cheer

indicators.note: the cheer breaks into the middle of the phrase for hypnotised

parts.note: someone hypnotised is in a trance
olé is the shout of a crowd at a bullfight

explanation.surface: A hypnotised spectator at a bullfight is roused by the crowd's shout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hypnotised' gives a two-word phrase, in a trance, run together; 'interrupted by' breaks it with the Spanish crowd's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being unable to endure or put up with something, such as a food or a view.

clue.text: Governess repeated names to absorb a youngster at first

indicators.note: the repeated name letters take in the single letter a

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name, written three times for the plural repeated

indicators.note: only the opening letter of youngster is used

explanation.surface: A governess keeps saying names so a young child will take them in.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside NNN to give NANN, then Y, the first letter of 'youngster', follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to look after and teach children in their home, close to a governess in role.

clue.text: Our pigsties could become well-regarded

indicators.note: the letters of the two words might be turned into something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A farmer hopes their humble pig pens might gain a fine reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something held in high esteem, carrying status and renown.

clue.text: Church more upset over US city service

indicators.note: in a down clue, the rearranged letters sit over, above, the city

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England

indicators.note: the letters of more are knocked over and rearranged

parts.note: NY is New York

explanation.surface: A church is unhappy about an American city's religious service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges MORE into REMO, which is placed 'over' NY.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal religious rite or service, such as a wedding.

clue.text: Stop including openings for university lecturers in consequence

indicators.note: the word for stop takes the opening letters inside it

parts.note: a rest is a stop or pause

indicators.note: the first letters of university and lecturers are taken

explanation.surface: Halting the hiring of university lecturers has a knock-on effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'openings for' takes the first letters of two words, and 'including' puts that pair inside the word for stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an outcome or effect that follows from an action.

clue.text: Corresponding mail is distributed on run

indicators.note: the letters are spread around and rearranged, as post is handed out

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Letters are being handed out on a postal round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: alike, matching or comparable in nature.

clue.text: Good old weapon getting a quick look

parts.note: a lance is a long spear used by medieval knights

explanation.surface: An antique weapon is given a brief once-over.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a brief or hurried glimpse at something.

clue.text: His place of work is mine

definitions.text: His place of work is mine

parts.words: His place of work is mine
parts.note: reads like a boss claiming the office, but mine is a coal pit, where this worker toils

explanation.surface: Someone possessively claims a man's workplace as their own.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal miner, a man whose workplace is the colliery underground.

clue.text: Coarser mind misinterpreted country pastime

indicators.note: the letters are read the wrong way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crude-thinking person has got the wrong idea about a rural hobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misinterpreted' rearranges COARSERMIND. Morris dancing is a traditional English folk dance with bells, sticks and handkerchiefs, performed at village fairs.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a traditional English folk dance associated with village life and the countryside.

clue.text: Revolutionary study about part of Bible is well-known

indicators.note: the turned word goes around the part of the Bible
the word for study is turned round, as in a revolution

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A radical study of a section of scripture becomes famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' turns the study round first, and 'about' then wraps the turned word around the Old Testament abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: famous, celebrated, widely recognised.

clue.text: Graduate on ship sees fish

parts.note: BA is Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A graduate on board a ship spots fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a sea bass is a fish caught for food.

clue.text: Exhausted, having nothing more to pay?

definitions.meaning: describing a price that includes everything, with no extras

explanation.surface: Someone is worn out but relieved there is no further bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated phrase means both tired out and inclusive of all charges, as in a package price.

clue.text: Band backed trio appearing without one conductor

indicators.note: the word for band is turned back to front

parts.note: a seam is a band, as of coal in rock

indicators.note: the word trio shows up lacking one letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A band supports a trio who perform without one member, under a music director.
explanation.walkthrough: SEAM reversed gives MAES; TRIO without I gives TRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A title given to a distinguished musical conductor or master musician.

clue.text: Police officer upset re agents

indicators.note: the letters are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A police officer is unhappy about secret agents.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank in the police above constable, so it names a kind of police officer.

clue.text: Limits to enraged guy expressing irritability

indicators.note: the boundary letters, first and last, of each of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: There are bounds to how much an angry man will show his temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: tense, nervous and on edge, showing irritation.
